steps.stem: For which of the following questions will a negative answer make it possible to determine with absolute certainty that every employee who does not drive to work lives within the city limits?
choices: Is there an employee who drives to work and does not live within the city limits?
Is there an employee who does not drive to work and does not live within the city limits?
Is there an employee who lives within the city limits and does not drive to work?
Is there an employee who does not live within the city limits and drives to work?
explanation: The claim fails only if some employee does not drive and does not live in the city; a "no" to (2) rules that out. (1) and (4) are about drivers, whom the claim does not mention; (3) asks about employees who fit the claim.

steps.stem: Three of the following claims have the same meaning. Which is the remaining claim?
choices: Every boat that has failed the safety test is not permitted to carry passengers
There is no boat that has failed the safety test and is permitted to carry passengers
If a boat is not permitted to carry passengers, it has failed the safety test
Only a boat that is not permitted to carry passengers can have failed the safety test
explanation: (1), (2) and (4) all say: failed the test → not permitted to carry passengers. (3) reverses the arrow (not permitted → failed).

steps.stem: A pair of claims is called "balanced" if each of the two claims can be inferred from the other. Which of the following pairs of claims is balanced?
choices: A. If the store is open, Dana is at work. B. If Dana is not at work, the store is not open.
A. There is someone who did not attend the meeting. B. There is no one who attended the meeting.
A. No painter in the group is without a studio. B. There are painters in the group who have a studio.
A. Every plant that is not watered wilts. B. Every plant that wilts is not watered.
explanation: B in (1) is A flipped and negated (the contrapositive), so each follows from the other. (4) reverses the arrow without negating; in (3) A does not guarantee that painters exist and B does not say all of them have a studio; (2) are different claims.

steps.stem: Given: the members of the Amber Quartet are left-handed violinists who live in Lisbon. Which of the following questions can be answered on the basis of this information?
choices: Do left-handed violinists live in other cities as well?
Is the Amber Quartet the only group of left-handed violinists in Lisbon?
Is every left-handed violinist who lives in Lisbon a member of the Amber Quartet?
Is it true that none of the left-handed musicians who live in Lisbon plays the violin?
explanation: The quartet's members exist and are left-handed musicians in Lisbon who play the violin, so the answer to (4) is "no". (3) runs the arrow backwards; (1) and (2) ask about other cities and other groups, which the information does not mention.

steps.stem: In every month in which the bakery launches a new type of bread, its advertising expenses rise, and consequently its profits for that month fall. Which of the following cases certainly contradicts the statement above?
choices: A month in which the advertising expenses did not rise, but profits fell
A month in which no new type of bread was launched, but profits fell
A month in which no new type of bread was launched, but advertising expenses rose
A month in which a new type of bread was launched, but profits did not fall
explanation: The statement says that a launch is followed by a fall in profits; (4) has the launch without the fall. The statement says nothing about months without a launch, so (1), (2) and (3) do not contradict it.

steps.stem:
Statement A: All top-floor apartments have balconies.
Statement B: All apartments without balconies are on lower floors.
The existence of a lower-floor apartment with a balcony -
choices: contradicts statement A but not statement B
does not contradict either statement
contradicts both statements
contradicts statement B but not statement A
explanation: A speaks about top-floor apartments and B about apartments without balconies; this apartment is neither, so neither statement says anything about it. (B is simply A flipped and negated.)

steps.stem:
Twelve hikers set out on a trail that leads to a lookout point. It is known that:
- every hiker who carried a map reached the lookout point;
- every hiker who reached the lookout point returned before sunset.
If so, it is not possible that one of the hikers -
choices: carried no map and returned after sunset
carried a map and returned before sunset
carried a map and returned after sunset
carried no map and returned before sunset
explanation: Map → lookout point → back before sunset, so a hiker with a map cannot return after sunset. The rules say nothing about hikers without a map, so (1) and (4) are possible; (2) is what the rules predict.

steps.stem:
Omer visited the town library. It is known that:
- of the books in the library, Omer leafed through all the books written in Spanish;
- all the books Omer leafed through are hardcovers.
If so, it is not possible that the library has a book that -
choices: is in Spanish and is a paperback
is in Italian and is a hardcover
is in Spanish and is a hardcover
is in Italian and is a paperback
explanation: In Spanish → Omer leafed through it → hardcover, so a Spanish paperback is impossible. The rules say nothing about Italian books, and (3) is what the rules predict.

steps.stem: Which of the following pieces of information would make it possible to establish with certainty that every tile in the warehouse that is not glazed was made in Portugal?
choices: All the tiles not made in Portugal are glazed
All the tiles made in Portugal are glazed
Every glazed tile was made in Portugal
None of the tiles made in Portugal are glazed
explanation: "Not made in Portugal → glazed" is the flipped-and-negated form of "not glazed → made in Portugal". (3) reverses the arrow; (2) and (4) describe the Portuguese tiles, not where the unglazed tiles come from.

steps.title: Claims - the rules to know
steps.intro: Turn every claim into an arrow from the condition to the result.

tables.title: Reading a claim
head: The claim says
Arrow
What follows
rows: All A are B · If A then B
There is no A that is B
Only A is B · B only if A
A if and only if B

tables.title: Working with claims
head: Task
How
rows: join them through a shared term
look for the condition, or the negated result

tips: 'Only' at the start - reverse the arrow.
'Only' or 'every' mid-sentence: find what comes first - that's the condition.

steps.stem:
Three claims are given:
A. Noga is taller than Liat.
B. Liat has no teammate who is taller than she is.
C. Noga and Liat are not teammates.
Which of the following is correct?
choices: Claim A necessarily follows from claims B and C together
Claim B necessarily follows from claims A and C together
Claim C necessarily follows from claims A and B together
None of the claims necessarily follows from the other two together
explanation: Noga is taller than Liat (A), and no teammate of Liat's is taller than her (B), so Noga cannot be her teammate (C). B and C leave Noga's height open, and A and C say nothing about Liat's other teammates.

steps.stem: Of the six instruments in a school's music room, three - the violin, the cello and the harp - are string instruments, and three - the flute, the trumpet and the drum - are not. Four students each took a different instrument from the room. What is certainly true of the instruments the students took?
choices: Exactly one of them is not a string instrument
At most one of them is a string instrument
Two of them are string instruments and two are not
At least one of them is a string instrument
explanation: Four different instruments cannot all come from the three that are not string instruments, so at least one is a string instrument. (1), (2) and (3) each fix a number that the data leave open.

steps.stem:
Keren: "It seems to me that the lake's water level was low this spring."
Avi: "Why do you think so?"
Keren: "Because the ferry began operating late this year."
Avi: "You are mistaken. ____."
Which of the following best completes Avi's words?
choices: If the water level is high in spring, the water warms early, and the ferry begins operating late only if the water warms late
If the water level is low in spring, the water warms early, and the ferry begins operating late only if the water warms late
If the ferry begins operating late, the water warms early, and a high water level causes the water to warm late
If the ferry begins operating early, the water warms early, and a low water level causes the water to warm late
explanation: In (2), a late ferry means the water warmed late, so it did not warm early, so the level was not low - the opposite of Keren's conclusion. (1) and (3) lead from a late ferry to a low level and support Keren; (4) never leads back from the ferry to the water level.

steps.stem:
At the Dekel community center, the following holds for every member of the youth group:
A. No member who plays in the orchestra also sings in the choir.
B. Every member who does not attend the pottery workshop sings in the choir.
If so, it is not possible that Yael, a member of the youth group, takes part in -
choices: the orchestra only
the pottery workshop and the orchestra
the choir and the pottery workshop
the pottery workshop only
explanation: Orchestra only means no pottery, so by B Yael sings in the choir, which A forbids for an orchestra player. Each of the other combinations satisfies both rules.

steps.stem: A relation between two people is called "symmetric" if, whenever it holds between the first and the second, it also holds between the second and the first. It is called "reflexive" if it holds between every person and themselves. For example, "is heavier than" is neither: if Dan is heavier than Ruth, Ruth is not heavier than Dan, and no one is heavier than themselves. Which of the following relations is both symmetric and reflexive?
choices: was born in the same month as
is a sibling of
is no heavier than
is the teacher of
explanation: Being born in the same month works in both directions and holds of everyone with themselves. "Is a sibling of" is symmetric only; "is no heavier than" is reflexive only; "is the teacher of" is neither.

steps.stem:
A hypothesis and two findings from two separate studies are presented below.
Hypothesis: the Arvan lizard lays its eggs only in sandy soil.
Finding A: in the lizard's region, only the coast has sandy soil.
Finding B: no Arvan lizard eggs have been found on the coast.
Which of the following claims is correct?
choices: Each of the findings on its own weakens the hypothesis
The combination of the two findings weakens the hypothesis
One of the findings supports the hypothesis, and the other weakens it
The combination of the two findings supports the hypothesis
explanation: If the lizard laid eggs only in sandy soil, then by A it would lay them only near the coast, and by B none are found there. Each finding alone is compatible with the hypothesis; only together do they conflict with it.

steps.stem: Rina invites only people who do not invite her. Gil invites only Rina. Gil is the only person Tal does not invite. Hence -
choices: Rina invites Gil and invites Tal
Rina invites Tal and does not invite Gil
Rina does not invite Gil and does not invite Tal
Rina invites Gil and does not invite Tal
explanation: Gil invites Rina, and Tal, who invites everyone except Gil, invites Rina too. Since Rina invites only people who do not invite her, she invites neither of them.

steps.stem: Dana is married to Ido, and she has exactly one brother-in-law. Which of the following is not possible?
choices: Dana has only brothers, and Ido has one brother, who is not married
Dana has two sisters, and one of them is married. Ido has only one sister
Dana has one sister. Ido is an only son
Dana has only sisters, and none of them is married. Ido is an only child
explanation: Dana's possible brothers-in-law are Ido's brothers and the husbands of her sisters (and, in a broader sense, the husbands of Ido's sisters). In (4) Ido has no siblings and none of Dana's sisters has a husband, so Dana has no brother-in-law at all. In each of the other cases exactly one can exist.

steps.stem:
There are three boxes on a shelf. Each box holds a ball and a cube. Each of the two objects can be either black or white. Given:
A. Only one of the cubes is white.
B. There are more black cubes than white balls.
Based on this information, it necessarily follows that -
choices: at least one box holds two white objects
there are more white objects than black objects
at least one box holds two black objects
if a box holds a black object, it also holds a white object
explanation: Two cubes are black (A), so there is at most one white ball (B), and at least two balls are black. Two black cubes and two black balls in three boxes must share a box. (2) and (4) are in fact impossible, and (1) may or may not be true.

steps.stem: If Dor is Eli's "marvek," and Eli is Fadi's "marvek," then Fadi cannot be Dor's "marvek." What could be the meaning of "marvek"?
choices: coworker
grandson
neighbor
competitor
explanation: If Dor is Eli's grandson and Eli is Fadi's grandson, Fadi is Dor's great-grandfather and cannot be his grandson. Coworkers, neighbors and competitors can form a closed circle of three.

steps.stem:
Each of the paintings shown at the Tamar Gallery's spring exhibition was painted by a single artist. It is known that at this exhibition:
A. All the paintings done in watercolor were by local artists.
B. All the paintings by foreign artists were for sale.
Which of the following best completes the sentence below?
Therefore, ____ that "Harbor at Dawn," an oil painting by a local artist that was for sale, was shown at the exhibition, since this ____.
choices: it is possible / does not contradict either statement
it is not possible / contradicts statement A
it is not possible / contradicts statement B
it is not possible / contradicts the combination of the two statements
explanation: A speaks only about watercolors and B only about foreign artists; an oil painting by a local artist is neither, so neither statement rules it out. "Local" and "for sale" merely echo the statements' results.

steps.stem:
Given:
- Old trees never bloom early.
- Early-blooming trees are the only ones that are pruned in winter.
Which of the following statements about the fig tree in Noam's garden is necessarily true?
choices: If it is pruned in winter, then it is not old
If it is not pruned in winter, then it is old
If it does not bloom early, then it is old
If it is not old, then it is not pruned in winter
explanation: Pruned in winter → blooms early → not old. (2) and (3) start from what is missing and draw a result the rules never give; (4) flips the arrow wrongly - the valid flip is "old → not pruned in winter."

steps.stem: A veteran mechanic claims that if a car's engine overheats - the red warning light comes on. Which of the following claims is equivalent to the mechanic's claim?
choices: If, and only if, a car's engine overheats - the red warning light comes on
A lit warning light always means an overheating engine, but an overheating engine does not necessarily turn the light on
An overheating engine always turns the warning light on, but a lit warning light does not necessarily mean an overheating engine
If, and only if, the red warning light comes on - the car's engine is overheating
explanation: The claim runs one way only: overheating → light. (3) says exactly that and denies the reverse. (1) and (4) add the reverse direction; (2) keeps only the reverse.

steps.stem:
Four musicians - Adi, Boaz, Carmela and Dov - auditioned for the city orchestra.
- Adi and Dov have each played professionally for more than five years.
- Boaz has played professionally for two years.
- Carmela has never played professionally.
The orchestra's announcement stressed that "candidates with less than five years of professional experience will not be accepted." If this rule is enforced, which of the following situations is not possible?
choices: Only Adi and Dov were accepted into the orchestra
Adi, Boaz and Carmela were not accepted into the orchestra
Dov was not accepted into the orchestra
Carmela and Adi were accepted into the orchestra
explanation: Carmela has no professional experience, so the rule excludes her. The rule only rules people out; it does not require anyone to be accepted, so (1), (2) and (3) are all possible.

steps.stem:
Hagit: "After a year of working with Oren, I have reached two conclusions about him. First, Oren would never turn down an assignment that involves travel. Second, Oren might accept an assignment that involves no travel."
Ravid: "Then one of your conclusions is wrong. I offered Oren an assignment that ____."
Which of the following would logically complete Ravid's words?
choices: involved travel, and he accepted it
involved no travel, and he turned it down
involved travel, and he turned it down
involved no travel, and he accepted it
explanation: Only a travel assignment that Oren refused contradicts the first conclusion. The second says only that he might accept; one refusal of a no-travel assignment does not refute it, and (1) and (4) fit both conclusions.

steps.stem:
A hotel hosted eight delegates: two from Spain, two from Chile, two from Kenya and two from Japan. The delegates stayed in four rooms. It is known that -
A. Each room was shared by two delegates.
B. No two delegates from the same country shared a room.
C. One of the rooms was shared by a delegate from Japan and a delegate from Spain.
Therefore, there must be -
choices: at least one room shared by a delegate from Kenya and a delegate from Chile
at least one room shared by a delegate from Chile and a delegate from Japan
more than one room shared by a delegate from Japan and a delegate from Spain
more than one room shared by a delegate from Kenya and a delegate from Chile
explanation: The other three rooms hold one Japanese, one Spanish, two Chilean and two Kenyan delegates. Only two of the four Chileans and Kenyans can be paired with the Japanese and the Spaniard, so at least one Chilean shares with a Kenyan. The other choices fail in some arrangement.

steps.stem: A book club has a rule about recommending books. It follows from the rule that Ayelet may recommend books to Boris but not to Carmel, while Carmel may recommend books to Ayelet but not to Boris. Which of the following could this rule be?
choices: A member may recommend books to all the members who are younger than they are, and only to them
A member may recommend books to all the members whom they themselves brought into the club, and only to them
A member may recommend books to all the members who live on their street, and only to them
A member may recommend books to all the members who read French, and only to them
explanation: Ayelet brought in Boris and Carmel brought in Ayelet, while Carmel did not bring in Boris - no conflict. With age, Boris would be younger than Carmel, so Carmel could recommend to him (1); living on the same street works both ways (3); reading French would have to be both true and false of Boris (4).

steps.stem:
- The heron greets only the frog.
- The otter trusts all the animals, except for the animals that the heron greets.
- The eagle envies all the animals, except for the animals that the otter trusts.
Therefore, the eagle -
choices: envies all the animals
envies only the frog
does not envy any animal
envies all the animals, except for the heron
explanation: The otter trusts every animal except the frog, so the only animal it does not trust - and the only one the eagle envies - is the frog.

steps.stem:
- Every judge is either a musician or a critic, but not both.
- All the guests are from abroad.
The addition of which of the following would lead to the conclusion that no guest is a judge?
choices: Anyone from abroad is a musician and a critic
Anyone who is not a judge is from abroad
Anyone who is a musician and a critic is from abroad
Anyone from abroad who is a critic is a musician
explanation: With (1), every guest is both a musician and a critic, which no judge can be. (3) reverses the needed arrow; (4) leaves room for a guest who is a musician only; (2) says nothing about the guests.

steps.stem:
Given:
- Only on the third floor are there offices with a balcony.
- Only offices with a balcony can have a coffee machine.
- Some corner offices have a coffee machine.
Which of the following conclusions does not follow from the information given?
choices: Some corner offices have a balcony
No office without a balcony has a coffee machine
Only corner offices have a balcony
Some corner offices are on the third floor
explanation: The corner offices with a coffee machine must have a balcony and be on the third floor, which gives (1), (2) and (4). Nothing rules out non-corner offices with a balcony, so (3) does not follow.

steps.stem: Taken together, the following four statements about the brothers Amit and Yoav contain a contradiction. Which statement could be omitted with the contradiction remaining?
choices: Yoav has read the novel "Glass Orchards."
There is no novel that Yoav has read and Amit has not read.
Only one of the brothers has read the novel "Glass Orchards."
Amit has read only one novel.
explanation: (1) and (2) mean that Amit has also read "Glass Orchards," which contradicts (3). The contradiction stands without (4); dropping any of the other three removes it.

steps.stem:
Statement A: Only in the museum's old wing are there halls without air conditioning.
Statement B: None of the halls in the old wing are air-conditioned.
Claim: If the map hall is air-conditioned, it is not in the old wing.
This claim follows -
choices: from statement A but not from statement B
only from the combination of the two statements
from statement B but not from statement A
from each of the statements separately
explanation: B says old wing → no air conditioning; flipped and negated, air conditioning → not in the old wing, which is the claim. A says no air conditioning → old wing, which says nothing about air-conditioned halls.

steps.stem: Rachel claimed that all the hardcover books in her shop were in English, and that she had no used books that were not signed by their author. Eli browsed the shop and found one book that disproved both claims. Which of the following cannot be the book Eli found?
choices: a paperback
a used book
a hardcover
a book not signed by its author
explanation: To disprove the first claim the book must be a hardcover not in English; to disprove the second it must be used and unsigned. So it is a hardcover and cannot be a paperback.

steps.stem:
It is known that some runners in the club are faster than Ilan.
Below are two statements:
A. Ilan is heavier than every runner who is faster than he is.
B. Ilan is faster than every runner he is heavier than.
Which of the following is true of the above statements?
choices: The two statements mean the same thing
The two statements contradict each other
Statement B necessarily follows from statement A
Statement A necessarily follows from statement B
explanation: Take a runner who is faster than Ilan. By A, Ilan is heavier than that runner; then by B, Ilan is faster than them - impossible. Because such a runner exists, the statements cannot both be true.

steps.stem:
Shai, a farmer, runs a sprinkler and a water pump according to the following rules:
- The sprinkler runs at night and is off during the day.
- The pump can run only when Shai is in the field.
- Shai is never in the field at night.
Which of the following situations is not possible?
choices: Shai is not in the field and the sprinkler is running
The pump and the sprinkler are both running
The pump is off and the sprinkler is running
The pump and the sprinkler are both off
explanation: If the pump runs, Shai is in the field, so it is daytime and the sprinkler is off. Each of the other situations fits some time of day.

steps.stem: Uri claims that every restaurant in town that is not near the sea is either noisy or expensive, but not both. The existence of which of the following restaurants proves that Uri is mistaken?
choices: A restaurant near the sea that is quiet and cheap
A restaurant far from the sea that is quiet and expensive
A restaurant near the sea that is noisy and expensive
A restaurant far from the sea that is quiet and cheap
explanation: Uri's claim covers only restaurants far from the sea, and requires exactly one of the two traits; (4) has neither. (1) and (3) are near the sea, and (2) fits the claim.

steps.stem:
At a certain moment, there are exactly four visitors at an amusement park's go-kart track: Avner, Batya, Gidi and Dalia.
Given:
- Avner is 11 years old.
- Batya is only watching.
- Gidi is 30 years old.
- Dalia is driving a go-kart.
Which of the following additional pieces of information makes it possible to determine that, at that moment, the rule strictly prohibiting anyone under the age of 14 from driving a go-kart was not broken?
choices: Avner is only watching and Gidi is driving a go-kart
Dalia is 13 years old and Avner is only watching
Batya is 10 years old and Gidi is driving a go-kart
Avner is only watching and Dalia is 16 years old
explanation: Only Avner (too young to drive) and Dalia (driving, age unknown) need checking; (4) settles both. (1) and (3) leave Dalia's age open, and in (2) the rule is broken.
